questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, makes it harder to concentrate, slows your reaction time, and reduces your coordination.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means drivers in the lane with the broken line can pass. Drivers in the lane with the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: When should you not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is against the law.

questions.question: You are driving behind a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Follow closely in bad weather because the truck driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Stay no more than one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too close to a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirror. This is dangerous. Stay farther back to give yourself time to stop if the truck brakes suddenly.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to or pulling away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or pulling away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when pulling up to a curb and when pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop wherever you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the road with all four wheels off the pavement if possible.

questions.question: How should head restraints be positioned?

options.text: Touching the back of your head.
Removed from the seats.
In any position, as they do not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Touching the back of your head.
questions.explanation: Head restraints prevent whiplash injuries if your car is hit from behind. They should touch the back of your head.

questions.question: What risk does fatigue increase?

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes driving errors and increases crash risk. When fatigued, you may fall asleep at the wheel and cause a serious crash.

questions.question: The road ahead is flooded. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded water. Even shallow water can hide dangers. Turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Bad weather makes it hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: In bad weather or darkness, increase the space between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to get better traction.
Press the brakes firmly to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain, your tires may lose contact with the road and ride on water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can drive in either direction in this lane.
Traffic is moving in both directions.
You are near a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in both directions.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is moving in both directions.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after stopping.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off your signal before finishing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping so other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your plans.

questions.question: When passing another car, when is it safe to move back into your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals for you to return.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: It is safe to return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror. This means there is enough distance between you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way traffic.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note attached to it with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn around and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and go with caution.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may confuse or scare them. Yield to them and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A train has passed at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.
Check for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not go until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: A school bus ahead is stopped to pick up or drop off children. What must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and a stop arm out, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is raised before moving. Even after the bus moves, check for children crossing before you go.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, and you could cause a crash.

questions.question: What often happens when you brake hard on ice and snow?

options.text: You stop faster.
The front wheels lock up, and you lose steering control.
The brakes stay from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front wheels lock up, and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front brakes, making you lose steering control. Slow down and drive carefully to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: Your vehicle starts to skid. What should you do?

options.text: Ease off the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as you can.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake to balance the vehicle again. Steer toward the direction of the skid to regain control.
